review_methods: Read complete final driver, all tests and operational deviation document.
Checked exclusive-write implementation, session addressing and frozen-input validation in unchanged dependencies.
Independently reran all 11 no-inference tests: 11 passed in 0.40s.
Checked canonical Astra result identifies the exact previously approved posthoc helper and matches recovery.json.
conclusions: Only absent destinations with completed actual predecessors are launchable; existing results and claims are preserved.
Both prelaunch-claimed lifecycles are censored in full, preserving twelve planned slots as unassessed.
Continuation overrides only exact original BrokenPipeError markers, preserves their bytes, and stops profiles on new failures.
The unchanged run_session retains original models, row order within each profile, tasks, package, corpus, bounds, isolation, receipts, retained state and grader.
Both stdout and stderr must be the declared regular log file before any phase claim or model launch. Detached logging survives a launcher exit in the real subprocess test.
An exclusive hash-bound phase claim prevents a second attempt by changing the output path; phase2 requires independent approval of the exact phase1 summary.
All frozen experiment inputs, approved continuation inputs, existing results and original failure files are checked before launch and between sessions. Shared input faults stop further launch.
Posthoc Astra status remains explicitly recovered with unknown OS exit and infrastructure fault; original surviving artifacts earned 30/30.
limitations: Operational recovery is a documented deviation from the original supervisor permanent profile block. Original failed checkpoint remains.
Two incomplete profile/family cells weaken matching: report planned and assessed denominators, complete-cell sensitivity, and recovered-cell-exclusion sensitivity.
Successful logging tests address the observed broken-pipe cause; they cannot guarantee absence of a future machine or host fault.
